headline: Nvidia posts blowout Q2 FY27: $96.2B revenue, guides Q3 to $108B
summary: Nvidia reported fiscal Q2 revenue of $96.22B (+105.8% YoY), beating the $92.07B consensus by 4.5%, with adjusted EPS of $2.22. Gross margin came in at 75.0%. Management guided Q3 FY27 revenue to $108B - an $11.8B sequential step - well above Street expectations. Shares jumped ~8% in after-hours trade on the print.

headline: Nvidia Data Center revenue hits $89B on Blackwell Ultra ramp
summary: Data Center accounted for $89.0B of Nvidia's Q2 FY27 revenue, roughly 92% of total, as hyperscale and enterprise customers accelerated Blackwell Ultra deployments. Nvidia flagged that gross margin will trough at 71-72% in Q4 FY27, partly on higher memory prices - a tailwind for HBM suppliers SK Hynix, Micron and Samsung.

headline: Nvidia takes $400M H200 charge as China sales stall; Q3 guide assumes zero China revenue
summary: Nvidia disclosed a ~$400M inventory charge tied to excess H200 chips as Chinese buyers backed away amid a 15% US-government revenue share arrangement and Beijing pushback. Management explicitly excluded any H20/H200 China revenue from the $108B Q3 guide, leaving upside optionality but underscoring the fragility of the China channel.

headline: Wall Street lifts Nvidia targets after print; Bernstein to $400, Raymond James to $352
summary: Analysts raised targets across the board following Nvidia's Q2 beat. Bernstein went to $400 (from $315, Outperform), Raymond James to $352 (from $330, Strong Buy), Morgan Stanley to $300 (from $288, Overweight), and Stifel also raised. Average consensus target now sits around $305 with 48 Strong Buy ratings.

headline: Goldman Sachs upgrades Broadcom to Buy, lifts target to $589
summary: Goldman Sachs analyst Toshiya Hari upgraded Broadcom to Buy from Neutral with a $589 price target (from $527), implying ~18% upside. The upgrade builds on Broadcom's guidance for AI semiconductor revenue to climb over 200% YoY to $16B this quarter and $30B+ in AI bookings flagged by CEO Hock Tan.

headline: CoreWeave lands multi-year AI cloud deal with Hudson River Trading; backlog hits $104B
summary: CoreWeave signed a multi-year GPU-compute deal with quantitative trading firm Hudson River Trading, extending its reach beyond hyperscaler and AI-lab customers into financial-market workloads. The company disclosed a ~$104B revenue backlog and is targeting more than 1.8 GW of active datacenter capacity by year-end 2026, up from ~1.5 GW today.

headline: Marvell Q2 preview: AI networking bookings and 76% datacenter mix in focus (reports today AMC)
summary: Marvell reports fiscal Q2 after the close today. Street consensus expects ~$2.7B in revenue; datacenter accounts for ~76% of the mix and management previously raised the FY27 interconnect growth outlook to over 70% YoY. Stock has run 187% YTD into the print - options market implies a large move.

headline: Samsung, SK Hynix accelerate 8-layer HBM4 shipments to Nvidia in H2 2026
summary: Samsung and SK Hynix are ramping 8-layer HBM4 shipments to Nvidia this year as Nvidia seeks a greater mix of 8-layer parts alongside 12-high for the next-gen Vera Rubin platform. Samsung's HBM4 yield has reportedly climbed to ~80% (from below 60% at ramp start), ahead of its year-end target - a positive read-through for its memory turnaround and for HBM pricing broadly.

headline: Centrus Energy raises FY2026 revenue guidance to $450-500M on HALEU demand
summary: Centrus Energy lifted its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $450-500M from a prior $425-475M range. The company is pursuing a multi-billion dollar Piketon, OH expansion to grow LEU and HALEU output and support $2.4B+ of contingent LEU sales commitments under definitive agreements - a direct read on advanced-reactor and SMR fuel demand.
